title: What to Know About the Banking Service Outages
author: Connor Greene
body:
Thousands of customers at multiple major U.S. banks are reporting difficulties accessing banking services on Monday after JPMorgan Chase announced a technical issue impacting its systems.

“JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems – there is no evidence this is cyber-related,” the company, which has over 86 million customers across the U.S., wrote on X. “It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.”

“We’re working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today,” it added.

JPMorgan Chase did not immediately respond to TIME’s request for additional information regarding the issue.

Here’s what we know.

Which banks and services are being impacted?

Beyond Chase, customers at several other banks—including Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Capital One, and Truist—have reported problems on Monday, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.com. Issues were also reported with digital money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase noted that other banks where it was “party to a transaction” may also be impacted by the technical issue it is experiencing. But it added that “this is not a systemic issue.”

The company also said that its customers retained access to their accounts and money.

Zelle said in a statement to news outlets that its service is "operating as it should," but that "an issue at the financial institutions may be impacting broader services, including Zelle payments, for some of their customers."

“Consumers use Zelle through participating banks and credit unions, which manage their accounts and hold their funds,” a spokesperson for the company said. “Consumers do not have a separate Zelle account, and Zelle does not hold consumer funds. An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers. Please contact them directly.”

Zelle is owned and operated by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which is itself jointly owned by financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank, and Capital One.

A U.S. Bank spokesperson said to multiple outlets that “U.S. Bank systems are not directly impacted,” but that “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”

How widespread are the outages?

Many Chase customers reportedly received a message on Monday that said “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

By around 2 p.m. Eastern time, more than 4,700 customers at the bank had reported experiencing problems, according to Downdetector.com.

Reports of issues at other banks spiked around the same time, with just over 2,000 outage reports at Bank of America and 1,060 at U.S. Bank, per the site. Hundreds of customers at Wells Fargo, Capitol One, Truist, and Zelle also reported issues Monday afternoon.
